\subsection*{Light --- Calls: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Programs.Light.Calls}.

\subsection*{Light --- Calls: Results}

\begin{definition}[Program meets a relation]
\lean{Light.Meets}
\label{Light.Meets}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Limits, Light.Program, Light.frame}
Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be a set of execution limits, let $P$ be a program, and let
$p,d,T\in\mathbb N$, $\mathrm{vals}\in\mathbb Z^{*}$, and $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$.
Let $R$ be a predicate on pairs consisting of an integer and a memory function $\mathbb
N\to\mathbb Z$. The program meets $R$ at position $p$ and depth parameter $d$ if there
is a statement body at position $p$ in $P$ and, starting from the state with local frame
initialized by $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory $\mu$, execution under limits $\mathrm{lim}$
can end after $T$ steps in a state whose location-zero value and memory satisfy $R$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Establishing a call from its body]
\lean{Light.Meets.of_body}
\label{Light.Meets.of_body}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Meets, Light.Stmt, Light.frame}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d,T$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{args}$ be a finite
list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be an initial memory, and let $Q$
be a predicate on an integer and a memory function. Suppose procedure $p$ in $P$ has
body $s$, and executing $s$ from the state whose locations are initialized by
$\mathrm{args}$ and whose memory is $\mu$ can finish within cost $T$ with output and
final memory satisfying $Q$. Then the call to procedure $p$ on $\mathrm{args}$ from
memory $\mu$ at depth $d$ meets cost bound $T$ and postcondition $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of a call bound]
\lean{Light.Meets.mono}
\label{Light.Meets.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends.mono, Light.Meets}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d,T,T'$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{vals}$ be a finite
list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be an initial memory, and let
$R,R'$ be predicates on an integer and a memory function. If a call to procedure $p$ on
$\mathrm{vals}$ from memory $\mu$ at depth $d$ meets cost bound $T$ and postcondition
$R$, if $T\le T'$, and if $R(r,\nu)$ implies $R'(r,\nu)$ for every output $r$ and memory
$\nu$, then the call meets cost bound $T'$ and postcondition $R'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Increasing the cost bound]
\lean{Light.Meets.mono_time}
\label{Light.Meets.mono_time}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Meets, Light.Meets.mono}
\difficulty{2}
Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d,T,T'$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{vals}$ be a finite
list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be an initial memory, and let $R$
be a predicate on an integer and a memory function. If the call to procedure $p$ on
$\mathrm{vals}$ from memory $\mu$ at depth $d$ meets cost bound $T$ and postcondition
$R$, and $T\le T'$, then it meets cost bound $T'$ with the same postcondition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling the cost bound]
\lean{Light.Meets.mono_const}
\label{Light.Meets.mono_const}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Meets, Light.Meets.mono_time}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d,c,c',S$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{vals}$ be a
finite list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be an initial memory, and
let $R$ be a predicate on an integer and a memory function. If the call to procedure $p$
on $\mathrm{vals}$ from memory $\mu$ at depth $d$ meets cost bound $cS$ and
postcondition $R$, and $c\le c'$, then it meets cost bound $c'S$ with the same
postcondition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Appending a program preserves a call bound]
\lean{Light.Meets.append}
\label{Light.Meets.append}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends.append, Light.Meets, Light.Program, Light.getElem?_append_of_eq_some}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ and $P'$ be programs, let $p,d,T$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{vals}$ be a
finite list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a memory function, and
let $R$ be a predicate on an integer and a memory function. If program $p$ in $P$,
called on inputs $\mathrm{vals}$ with initial memory $\mu$ and depth parameter $d$, can
execute within cost $T$ and produce an output and final memory satisfying $R$, then the
same call in the concatenated program $P$ followed by $P'$ can do so as well.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cost bound for a procedure call]
\lean{Light.Ends.callLast}
\label{Light.Ends.callLast}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Ends.call, Light.Ends.mono, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.cost, Light.Expr.val, Light.Meets}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a program with resource limits $\mathrm{lim}$, a procedure name $p$, depth $d$,
argument expressions $\mathrm{args}$, a target local variable $x$, an initial local-variable
map $\mathrm{loc}$, initial memory $\mu$, and time bounds $T,T\prime$. Suppose the
procedure body for $p$, run at depth $d+1$ with argument values $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory
$\mu$, has an execution of cost at most $T\prime$ ending with result $r$ and memory
$\mu\prime$ satisfying $R(r,\mu\prime)$. Suppose every such result and memory yields
a state with local-variable map updated at $x$ to $r$ and memory $\mu\prime$ that
satisfies $Q$. If each argument expression is safe in the initial state and the arguments
evaluate to $\mathrm{vals}$, $d<\mathrm{lim.depth}$, and the sum of their evaluation
costs plus $2+T\prime$ is at most $T$, then the call to $p$ with those arguments,
assigning its result to $x$, has an execution of cost at most $T$ ending in a state
satisfying $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Call followed by a statement]
\lean{Light.Ends.callThen}
\label{Light.Ends.callThen}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Ends.callLast, Light.Ends.next, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.cost, Light.Expr.val, Light.Meets}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a program with limits $\mathrm{lim}$, procedure $p$, continuation statement $s$,
depth $d$, argument expressions $\mathrm{args}$, target variable $x$, local-variable map
$\mathrm{loc}$, initial memory $\mu$, and time bounds $T,T\prime$. Suppose the body of
$p$ at depth $d+1$, with argument values $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory $\mu$, has an
execution of cost at most $T\prime$ ending with result $r$ and memory $\mu\prime$
satisfying $R(r,\mu\prime)$. For every such $r,\mu\prime$, suppose $s$ executes from
the state whose local-variable map is updated at $x$ to $r$ and whose memory is
$\mu\prime$, within the remaining budget $T-(\sum_{e\in\mathrm{args}}\mathrm{cost}(e)+2+T\prime)$,
and ends in a state satisfying $Q$. Assume each argument expression is safe in the initial
state and the arguments evaluate to $\mathrm{vals}$, $d<\mathrm{lim.depth}$, and the sum
of the argument evaluation costs plus $2+T\prime$ is at most $T$. Then the call to $p$
with arguments $\mathrm{args}$, assigning its result to $x$, followed by $s$, executes
from the initial state within cost $T$ and ends in a state satisfying $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Procedure call with a bounded execution]
\lean{Light.Ends.callTo}
\label{Light.Ends.callTo}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Ends.callLast, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.cost, Light.Expr.val, Light.Meets, Light.frame, Light.setLocal, Light.update_frame_setLocal}
\difficulty{2}
Let $P$ be a program, let its execution limits be given, and let $d,p,x,T,T'$ be natural
numbers, $l$ and $\mathrm{vals}$ finite lists of integers, and $\mu$ a memory function
from natural numbers to integers. Suppose procedure $p$ has a body that, when started at
depth $d+1$ with local frame initialized from $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory $\mu$, has an
execution of cost at most $T'$ whose final value and memory satisfy $R(r,\mu')$. Assume
every pair $(r,\mu')$ satisfying $R$ makes the state with memory $\mu'$ and local frame
obtained by setting position $x$ of $l$ to $r$ satisfy $Q$. If each expression in the
call's argument list is safe in the state with local frame initialized from $l$ and
memory $\mu$, and those expressions evaluate to $\mathrm{vals}$; if $d$ is less than the
depth limit; and if the sum of the argument expression costs plus $2+T'$ is at most $T$,
then the call to procedure $p$ with those arguments, storing its returned value at
position $x$, has an execution of cost at most $T$ from that state to a state satisfying
$Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Procedure call followed by a statement]
\lean{Light.Ends.callToThen}
\label{Light.Ends.callToThen}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Ends.callTo, Light.Ends.next, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.cost, Light.Expr.val, Light.Meets, Light.frame, Light.setLocal}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a program with limits $\mathrm{lim}$, procedure $p$, continuation $s$, depth $d$,
target local index $x$, time bounds $T,T\prime$, a local-variable list $l$, argument
values $\mathrm{vals}$, and initial memory $\mu$. Suppose the body of $p$ at depth $d+1$,
with local frame initialized from $\mathrm{vals}$ and memory $\mu$, has an execution of
cost at most $T\prime$ ending with result $r$ and memory $\mu\prime$ satisfying
$R(r,\mu\prime)$. For every such $r,\mu\prime$, suppose $s$ executes from the state
with local frame obtained by setting index $x$ of $l$ to $r$ and memory $\mu\prime$,
within the remaining budget $T-(\sum_{e\in\mathrm{args}}\mathrm{cost}(e)+2+T\prime)$,
and ends in a state satisfying $Q$. Assume every argument expression is safe in the
state with local frame $l$ and memory $\mu$, and the argument expressions evaluate there
to $\mathrm{vals}$. If $d<\mathrm{lim.depth}$ and the argument evaluation costs plus
$2+T\prime$ sum to at most $T$, then the call to $p$ with those arguments, storing its
result at index $x$, followed by $s$, executes from the state with local frame $l$ and
memory $\mu$ within cost $T$ and ends in a state satisfying $Q$.
\end{theorem}
